anomalies.observed: No real-time-clock IC (PCF85063 or any equivalent 6/8-pin RTC) is drawn anywhere in the schematic. The complete flat sheet (cm4-robot.kicad_sch, Id 1/1) contains only these I2C/I2C-SPI devices: U26 PCA9536D (GPIO expander), U31 LSM6DS3 (IMU), U32 LIS3MDL (magnetometer), U33 ADS1115IDGS (the 'I2C Address 0x48' part is the ADC, not an RTC), U17 ET6226M (display driver) and U13/U14 SC16IS752 (UARTs). The CM4 module symbol (Module1A/1B) is a connector and does not contain an RTC.
anomalies.expected: The specification states, as a fact taken from the reference schematic/netlist, that the board implements an RTC: 'Compute carrier: hosts the CM4 (Module1), breaking out GPIO, Ethernet, USB, camera connectors, and an RTC (datasheet link in cm4_robot_board/docs points to a PCF85063ATAAZ RTC — see new_notes.txt).' A PCF85063 (or equivalent) on the SCL6/SDA6 bus should therefore be present.

evidence.quote: TL;DR §1: 'Compute carrier: hosts the CM4 (Module1), breaking out GPIO, Ethernet, USB, camera connectors, and an RTC (datasheet link in cm4_robot_board/docs points to a PCF85063ATAAZ RTC — see new_notes.txt).'
Motion Sensing page (sheet 1, cols 12-13): U33 'ADS1115IDGS' with note 'I2C Address 0x48'; no PCF85063/RTC symbol appears on any sheet.

anomalies.impact: The board loses the real-time-clock function the reference design provides: no battery-backed calendar/timekeeping, so timestamps and any RTC-dependent scheduling/boot behaviour are absent compared with the intended design.

parsed.summary: Every concrete hardware fact the spec states is satisfied by the drawing (Y1/Y2 are 16 MHz, D9/D10 are the SM712 TVS arrays, U6 is the LTC4412xS6, the four SN74LVC1G07 e-stop buffers and the ISL54222 mux U5 are present, and GLOBAL_EN is tied straight to SW1 pin 2), so the documented open issues (RS-485-vs-CAN README mismatch, USB ideal-diode, GLOBAL_EN sequencing, LED polarity, camera connectors) are not anomalies. The one deviation the drawing supports is the absence of the PCF85063 RTC that the spec lists as implemented, which I report at moderate confidence.

Pin 1 = A (input), pin 2 = /OE (output enable), pin 3 = GND, pin 4 = Y (output), pin 5 = VCC.

Actually if you want the output to sink when /OE is low, then /OE low means enabled (output follows input). If input A is tied low, then output = low = sinking.
